key_insight: A structured LLM workflow (HeLIX) matched physician-level performance for extracting complex hepatology data from unstructured clinical notes.
clinical_relevance: This suggests AI could speed up cohort building, registry creation, and retrospective research by reducing manual chart review burden.
method: Prospective validation on 50 simulated hepatology discharge summaries
LLM used zero-shot structured chain-of-thought prompting with clinical reasoning, schema enforcement, and evidence verification
Compared 45 extracted variables against consensus manual chart review
evidence_signal: Across 2,250 data points, the model achieved 99.24% extraction accuracy, 0.98 F1 for binary variables, and 2 hallucinations (0.08%).
watch_item: Results came from simulated hepatology summaries, so real-world performance and safety need validation across other specialties and messy EHR contexts.
paper_title: General-purpose large language models can achieve physician-level accuracy in complex medical data extraction
